preamble: In languages with back/front vowel harmony, the velar stop /ɡ/ is retracted to a uvular [ɢ] in back-vowel words. In Khalkha Mongolian [ɢ] occurs before back vowels, and /ɡ/ and /ɢ/ contrast only at the end of back-vowel (−ATR) morphemes. In Turkmen, /ɡ, k, l/ have back allophones [ɢ, q, ɫ] in back-vowel words. Most Turkic languages instead have a fricative [ʁ] here, so the stop outcome is uncommon.

examples.note: Uvular realization before a back vowel.
Uvular in a back-vowel word, with the preceding nasal assimilating to [ɴ].
/ɡ/ is realized as uvular [ɢ] in back-vowel words; it spirantizes to [ʁ] intervocalically and next to obstruents.
